title: Greet with a default greeting
description: Write a function `greet(name, greeting="Hello")` that returns the string `"{greeting}, {name}!"`. If no `greeting` is provided by the caller, it should default to `"Hello"`.
hints: A function parameter can have a default value that is used automatically when the caller doesn't supply that argument.
You can build the result with an f-string, e.g. `f"{greeting}, {name}!"`.
Return an f-string of the form `f"{greeting}, {name}!"`; since `greeting` already defaults to `"Hello"` in the signature, you don't need any extra conditional logic in the body.
expected_behavior: Returns "{greeting}, {name}!", using the default greeting "Hello" when the caller does not pass one.
explanation: Giving `greeting` a default value of `"Hello"` in the function signature means callers can omit it entirely, and Python fills it in automatically. The f-string then formats whichever greeting was ultimately used together with `name`.
